parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing exposure is documented: the male-sodomy sections are unenforced (no prosecutions recorded), reach a trans visitor only tangentially, and no border, document, facility, custody or care rule is sourced at all. Structural signals extrapolate positively — no trans-specific offence, no documented police or societal targeting, and a locally recognized third-gender cultural role. Offsetting this: no general SOGI non-discrimination protection, employment-only enforcement judged poor, a decade-old climate record, and unresolved questions on entry documents. Per rule 13, latent tangential statute plus open questions and thin recourse sits a step below acceptance-with-working-protections, not a tier below.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No entry, visa, marker or document-mismatch rule is sourced; nothing shows foreign documents doubted or trans visitors screened.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No acceptance of X markers or chosen names is sourced either.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown document handling could interact with hotel registration or police ID checks, but no such interaction appears in the record.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 153-155 carry up to 14 years for male anal intercourse, but are sexuality not gender provisions, are unenforced (no prosecutions recorded), and no trans-specific arrest or custody practice is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented non-enforcement: 2015 report recorded zero prosecutions and no LGBTQ prosecutions reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A trans visitor could only reach these sections via alleged sexual conduct with a male partner; no case or police practice linking them to gender presentation is sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility, ward, custody-placement or birth-sex rule exists in the record for any level of government.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The record contains no subnational content at all, so no parent-subnational interaction can be traced.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. Gender-affirming care, HRT import, emergency-care refusal and insurance treatment are all unsourced for this jurisdiction.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking could interact with document checks, but no such pathway is evidenced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing toward gender diversity is documented. Constitution omits SOGI grounds and the considered anti-discrimination bill is unresolved — resident-facing gaps, not visitor exposure.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Government voted in 2016 to retain the UN SOGI Independent Expert mandate and was considering SOGI anti-discrimination legislation; a recognized third-gender cultural role signals social framing as oddity, not threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutional openness coexists with an unenforced sodomy statute; the statute shows no use as a police lever against gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule on minors, family travel, custody or accompanied children appears in the record.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not applicable — nothing links child presence to identification, accommodation or scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific violence, harassment, extortion or police targeting. The only climate figure — no societal discrimination or violence in 2015 — is a decade old and not current evidence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The 2015 observation and the absence of any recorded incident are weak positives; a 2014 study documents a locally legible gender-diverse role.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Foreigner status and cultural legibility may reduce friction, but no source tests this.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general SOGI non-discrimination statute; constitutional grounds exclude SOGI; employment protection (Art. 107(2)(b)) names sexual orientation only, gender discrimination poorly enforced. Thin formal recourse, but no documented traveler denied remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Employment protection exists for SOGI-adjacent claims; government signaled openness at UPR; no documented instance of refused complaint handling.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions — current status of sections 153-155, whether the anti-discrimination bill passed, post-2015 social climate — remain unanswered; per rubric these are light, not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above: Ostravia mandates universal hotel reporting of transgender guests with eviction and frozen funds — a continuous traveler-facing exposure with no effective remedy. This dossier documents no registration, reporting, eviction or inspection duty at any point of the journey, only silence on those axes and an unenforced, tangential statute.

Similar tier: Meridia offers trained border staff and a tribunal for detained visitors, while this jurisdiction documents no procedural protections at all. But Meridia also records real secondary screening and inconsistent officer discretion as exposures; this record shows neither. Slightly higher on exposure, lower on documented remedies — nets to about the same level.

Higher: Brindleport shows operative anti-discrimination ordinances, a functioning labor inspectorate, identity-based shelter placement and enforced remedies. This jurisdiction has a culturally recognized third-gender role but no general SOGI protection, poor enforcement of the gender-employment rule, and a ten-year-old climate record. Missing working machinery, plus unresolved entry-document questions, keeps it below the 0.85 band.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of documented absence rather than documented danger. The only criminal provisions on the record target male-male sex, are unenforced, and have no documented use against gender presentation; no border, facility, custody or care rule reaches a trans visitor. Positives carry real weight: zero recorded prosecutions, no documented targeting, a government voting to retain the UN SOGI expert mandate, and an embedded third-gender cultural role that makes a gender-diverse visitor locally legible rather than threatening. Negatives are mostly resident-facing gaps (narrow constitutional grounds, employment-only protection judged poorly enforced) or open questions (post-2015 climate, current statute status, document practice) which the rubric weights lightly. An adult alone or with a minor therefore faces no evidenced tier-1 or tier-2 exposure; stale data and thin recourse justify stopping short of the 0.80+ band.
